item.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia to level Liga leaders Barca
item.description: Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday. Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions. Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappe added a third in the second half. Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban. Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25. In the ninth minutes the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday. Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area. Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control. Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free-kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan. Guler soon doubled the lead, after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path. Guler had a good chance for the third in early in the second half but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him. Minutes later Dimitrievski saved well from Mbappe as the French striker ran through and tried to dink the ball over him. Bellingham powered his way through the defence and was also denied by the goalkeeper, as was Mbappe following up with an overhead kick, as Madrid tried to find a third to kill off the game. Eventually Mbappe produced it, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign. It was the forward’s 17th goal in 16 games across all competitions. Mbappe has netted in his last seven appearances for Madrid. Valencia’s Jose Gaya was dismissed with around 10 minutes remaining for a late sliding foul on Mbappe to further spoil Javier Aguirre’s team’s night. Earlier new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia’s side were held to a goalless home draw by Deportivo La Coruna. Osasuna snatched a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander came from behind to beat Malaga 2-1. item.title: ‘You’ve written your names in gold,’ Tinubu celebrates Flamingos, U-17 FIFA World Cup winners
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s Flamingos for making history as the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup following their 2-1 victory over Japan in Saturday’s final in Rabat, Morocco. Read Also: Nigeria’s Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win first U-17 Women’s World Cup The President, who received the cheering news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States, hailed Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the nation and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. “What wonderful news to return home to! Our young girls have conquered the world and given Nigerians everywhere another reason to celebrate our great country. “To our gallant Flamingos, I say congratulations. You have shown courage, discipline, determination and the Nigerian spirit of never giving up. “I followed your journey throughout this tournament, and after your semi-final victory, you promised to bring the trophy home. Today, you have kept that promise. You believed in yourselves, fought for one another and carried our nation’s flag to the very top of the world. “Your victory is an inspiration to millions of young Nigerian girls who dream of achieving greatness. You have shown them that with hard work, opportunity and determination, they too can reach the highest levels of achievement. “Today, Nigeria celebrates you. You have written your names in gold, and your country is immensely proud of you.” The President particularly applauds Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, whose goals secured the historic victory, while commending the entire squad for their exceptional teamwork throughout the tournament. He also congratulates the coaching crew, the Nigeria Football Federation and the National Sports Commission for their contributions to the team’s success. President Tinubu reaffirms his administration’s commitment to investing in grassroots sports development and expanding opportunities for young Nigerians, particularly girls, to discover, nurture and fulfil their potential. “Congratulations once again, Flamingos. Thank you for making Nigeria proud.” Vanguard News The post ‘You’ve written your names in gold,’ Tinubu celebrates Flamingos, U-17 FIFA World Cup winners appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gas transportation network not responsible for power generation drop – NNPC
item.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has said its gas transportation network remains available to supply gas to power generating stations nationwide, insisting that transportation constraints are not responsible for the current decline in electricity generation. The national oil company said operational records of its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited (NGIC), showed no transportation-related constraints within its network that could explain the drop in power generation. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja on Friday. The clarification followed a November 5 statement by the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which attributed the decline in electricity generation partly to limited gas availability and reduced water inflows into hydroelectric power stations. However, NNPC said its clarification was specifically about the operational status of its gas transportation infrastructure, noting that gas production, commercial supply arrangements and actual deliveries to individual power plants were separate issues requiring independent assessment. The company said gas production had grown by about 10 per cent year-to-date in 2026, attributing the increase to the Federal Government’s gas development and monetisation agenda. “Gas supply availability is therefore not a challenge as NNPC remains committed to supporting efforts to improve electricity generation through safe, reliable and efficient gas supply and transportation,” the statement said. NNPC further explained that determining the causes of the generation shortfall required an assessment of other components of the gas-to-power value chain. These, it said, included the availability and operational readiness of generating units, plant maintenance schedules and actual gas offtake by power stations. The company stressed that the factors must be examined alongside gas supply data to establish the specific causes of the decline in electricity generation. It also called for a coordinated review of operational data by gas suppliers, transporters, power generators and NISO to identify constraints and guide appropriate interventions. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to developing dependable energy infrastructure and collaborating with stakeholders to translate the country’s gas resources into more reliable electricity supply for Nigerians. item.title: Olawepo-Hashim visits Sowore, condemns political violence
item.description: Former presidential candidate, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has condemned political violence in Nigeria, warning that attacks on political opponents could worsen the country’s already precarious security situation. Olawepo-Hashim also called on President Bola Tinubu to caution members of his team against actions and statements capable of provoking political conflict. He made the remarks in a statement posted on his X platform on Saturday after visiting activist and publisher, Omoyele Sowore, following the reported attack on him in Ekiti State. Olawepo-Hashim said his visit was motivated by their longstanding relationship, which dates back to their participation in the struggle against military dictatorship and the campaign for democracy. He warned that Nigeria, already grappling with terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other security challenges, could not afford another crisis arising from political violence. “Nigeria cannot afford to add political violence to the general insecurity in the land. “Nigeria is already battling terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and widespread insecurity. We cannot afford to add political violence to this burden,” he said. The former presidential candidate welcomed a statement by a United Nations representative expressing concern over the incident and urged other international partners to condemn political violence. He also urged political leaders to exercise restraint, warning that those who provoke violence might not be the ones to suffer its consequences. “President Bola Tinubu must call his team to order. Political leaders must exercise restraint and stop actions or rhetoric capable of provoking conflict. Those who recklessly provoke violence may not be the ones who bear its consequences,” he said. Recalling their history, Olawepo-Hashim said he and Sowore had been comrades since 1989/1990, when they worked together against military rule. He said he was particularly moved by Sowore’s recollection of how he introduced him to political activism at the University of Lagos. According to him, Sowore reaffirmed during the visit that he remained undeterred by the reported attack and was determined to continue campaigning for genuine democracy. Olawepo-Hashim stressed that political disagreements should not be used as justification for violence, urging Nigerians to uphold democratic values and reject actions capable of worsening insecurity and instability in the country. item.title: Trump orders Justice Department probe of Democrats seeking impeachment
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration. Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterms. Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. “The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. “This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable,” he said, arguing that there had been “no impeachable acts committed.” Trump said he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act” and said “imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS.” With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Likely subjects include the Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. “Lawyer up,” wrote incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia on X as the results became clear on election night. Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles. Democrats could pursue Trump’s third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate — far beyond the party’s numbers. item.title: Atiku to Tinubu: 2027 conversation is how to repair damage your govt caused
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has told President Bola Tinubu that his administration’s failures will cost him re-election in 2027, challenging him to defend his record in office rather than attack his investment in education. Read Also: * Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP * Any Nigerian that’s not lazy will have food on the table – Yari Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, said Nigerians had endured enough hardship under Tinubu’s leadership, insisting that the next presidential election would be about reversing the damage “inflicted on the country through rising poverty, insecurity, unemployment and a crushing cost-of-living crisis”. In a statement on Saturday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku also defended his investment in the American University of Nigeria, AUN, insisting that his educational venture began before he became Vice President in 1999. “The answer is simple: my investment in education predates my time in public service. “In 1993, I was laying the foundation for ABTI Academy. That Academy has since grown into the American University of Nigeria,” Atiku said. He accused Tinubu of attempting to undermine his record in education because he could account for his own business and political journey. Turning to the economy, the former Vice President said Tinubu had no business seeking another mandate when millions of Nigerians were struggling with the consequences of his policies. “A president who has plunged the country into a crushing cost-of-living crisis has no business asking Nigerians for another mandate. The real conversation about the 2027 election is how to repair the damage your government has done,” Atiku said. He also challenged the President’s insistence that Nigeria could not return to fuel subsidy, questioning the benefits of the economic reforms to ordinary Nigerians. “You say Nigeria cannot return to subsidy and must move forward. But you cannot even tell Nigerians where you are taking them. Forward into deeper poverty, mounting debt, insecurity and mass unemployment?” he asked. item.title: Nigeria’s Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win first U-17 Women’s World Cup
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, have defeated Japan 2-1 to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Flamingos secured the historic victory on Saturday at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat, to claim their first title in the competition. Awawu Bashiru opened the scoring for Nigeria in the 39th minute with a long-range effort that slipped through the hands of the Japanese goalkeeper. Nigeria doubled their advantage shortly after the restart, with Oluebube Umejiaku finding the net in the 47th minute to put the Flamingos in control. Japan fought back and reduced the deficit through Fuki Ito in the 80th minute. The Japanese side pushed for an equaliser, but Nigeria held on to secure the 2-1 victory. The Flamingos also came close to extending their lead late in the game, striking the crossbar from a corner kick. Road to victory Flamingos’ campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. item.title: EPL: Delap double condemns Man City to third straight defeat
item.description: Manchester City slumped to a third consecutive Premier League defeat on Saturday as Liam Delap’s double lifted Nottingham Forest out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win at the City Ground. Oliver Glasner’s men had not scored at home at all this season, but pounced on City’s defensive errors to strike twice in the first 20 minutes through Jair Cunha and Delap. Rayan Cherki’s stunning strike gave City hope, but their title challenge is rapidly wilting even before the potential effects of a major points deduction. Delap sealed just Forest’s second win of the season with an incredible strike in off the post on the night that could launch his career for the two-time European champions, after a difficult start since his club-record £50 million ($67 million) move from Chelsea. Defeat leaves City six points adrift of leaders Arsenal and with questions over whether the uncertainty surrounding the club is playing a part in their on-field slump. Found guilty on over 100 Premier League charges of breaking financial rules, the 10-time English champions face a severe points penalty unless they can overturn that verdict on appeal. Glasner warned his players he would make big changes after a disappointing start to his reign saw them start the match in the bottom three. The Austrian got the response he craved as Forest burst out of the blocks to pounce on City’s sloppiness at the back. – Clinical Forest – Cunha robbed Josko Gvardiol midway inside the City half and was allowed to bear down on goal before slotting past Gianluigi Donnarumma. Forest’s first home goal in 511 minutes was celebrated wildly at the City Ground with owner Evangelos Marinakis jumping out of his chair in celebration. Elliott Anderson had a night to forget on his first return to Forest since a reported £116 million move to City. Xaver Schlager beat Anderson to the ball in midfield and set Delap running from inside his own half before unleashing an unstoppable drive past Donnarumma for his first home goal for the club. However, he has been hit with the task of trying to keep his players motivated when they do not know if they will even be in the English top-flight next season. Maresca showed his frustration with a double change at half-time with the introduction of Nico O’Reilly and Matheus Nunes helping to spark a brief City rally. item.title: ‘Huge dream’ to play for England with Jude – Jobe Bellingham
item.description: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham said Saturday he hoped to fulfil a “huge dream” by playing alongside brother Jude after being called up to the England squad. On Friday, England manager Thomas Tuchel named Jobe, 21, in England’s 25-man squad for November’s Nations League fixtures with Croatia and Spain. Speaking after Dortmund’s 2-1 home win over Elversberg in the Bundesliga, Jobe said he and brother had acted out playing together for England when they were kids. “It’s really good. I don’t want to get too carried away, but it’s obviously a big dream for me and for Jude as well,” the younger Bellingham told DAZN. “Since we were young, we reenacted that so many times in the garden or wherever, in the park, playing for England together. “So it’s a huge dream. It’s not happened yet, so I don’t want to jinx or say it too early, but yeah, I’m really excited.” Jobe has captained England’s under-21s but this is his first senior call-up. Real Madrid midfielder Jude, 23, who also made his England debut while playing for Dortmund, now has 60 England caps. Jobe took time to adapt to the Bundesliga since joining in 2025 but has impressed this season and has become an established member of Dortmund’s starting XI. Speaking on Friday, Dortmund coach Niko Kovac praised Jobe’s development and dedication to improving his game. “He is really a complete football freak. He studies his own game and the games of other players to learn from the best in his position. “And he’s a really great lad and he’s got an excellent attitude. I’m really happy for him that he can now wear the jersey of his national team next to his brother. “It’s something quite special, not just to play for your country, but to play alongside your brother. It’s incredible.” Vanguard News The post ‘Huge dream’ to play for England with Jude – Jobe Bellingham appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How Adeboye ordered return of billions traced to RCCG within 24 hours — EFCC boss
item.description: By Olayinka Latona The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, ordered the return of billions of Naira traced to church projects from an individual under investigation for alleged financial crimes within 24 hours, the Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, Ola Olukoyede, has said. Olukoyede said Adeboye gave the directive immediately after the commission briefed him on the investigation and the discovery that proceeds of the alleged financial crimes had been traced to some RCCG projects. The EFCC chairman disclosed this while addressing church workers and ministers after the monthly Holy Ghost Service at the Redemption City of God, Simawa, Ogun State. The programme, held at the invitation of Adeboye, had as its theme, “Ethical Standard and Corruption in Christian Community.” Recounting the incident, Olukoyede said the individual under investigation was involved in financial transactions worth tens of billions of naira, some of which the commission traced to the church. He said he personally approached Adeboye to explain the findings, adding that the cleric reacted angrily and immediately directed church officials to return the funds. “The reaction on the face of Daddy was like I was almost blaming myself for taking the matter to him. Daddy was visibly angry. He called one or two pastors and said, ‘I give you 24 hours. Everything you have traced to RCCG from this particular person who has been indicted, return it within the next 24 hours’. “That money was returned to the coffers of government. That is what RCCG is known for. That is who we are. We are not the custodian of proceeds of crime,” he said. Olukoyede commended Adeboye for what he described as his integrity, holiness and zero tolerance for corruption, contrasting his response with the alleged handling of a similar situation by another unnamed mega church. He claimed that individuals accused of fraud had operated an investment scheme through the other church, resulting in billions of naira being lost by members. “That is the difference between us and the others. Daddy Adeboye took action immediately he heard about the financial issue when the others are trying to defend it, justify it. Don’t justify processes of crime; it’s a crime to do that,” he said. Olukoyede, who is also a senior pastor in the RCCG, made the disclosure while addressing church workers and ministers after the monthly Holy Ghost Service at the Redemption City of God, Simawa, Ogun State. The programme, held at the invitation of the General Overseer of RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, had as its theme, “Ethical Standard and Corruption in Christian Community.” Recounting the incident, the EFCC chairman said he had no option but to authorise the detention of the senior cleric because of the evidence available to the commission, stressing that the alleged misconduct did not involve the pastor’s activities in the church. “I say this with every sense of humility. It was a day that I had calls to detain a very senior pastor in this mission. I had no choice. I needed to do it because of what we have seen. “Not because of his activities, what he perpetrated within the church, no. But because of what happened in his place of work, where he works in his secular activities. I feel things like this should not be happening within the Christian community,” he said. Olukoyede warned church leaders against using the pulpit to promote materialism and questionable sources of wealth, saying the church must not give undue recognition to individuals suspected of involvement in financial crimes. He said churches should welcome everyone but must not celebrate or elevate people whose wealth was linked to criminal activities. “Some of us pervert holiness on our altars. We don’t preach as much holiness as we do of materialism. It must not be seen in our parishes giving front row to criminals. “We are not saying we should send them away, but we must not use the altar to promote financial fraudulent activities. item.title: Delta Political Tension: Injuries, destruction as another Obi-Kwankwaso rally comes under attack
item.description: NDC fingers APC over attacks Baseless allegation with no proof — APC By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — Political tension heightened in Delta State on Saturday as supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), backing the presidential ambition of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, came under attack during a one-million-man march in Asaba, leaving several persons injured and campaign vehicles vandalised. The incident, which came after a similar disruption of the movement’s rally in Effurun, Delta State, reportedly involved suspected thugs armed with sticks, knives, machetes and other dangerous weapons. The vehicles, many branded with campaign banners bearing the images of Obi, his running mate, Kwankwaso, and the NDC candidate for Delta North Senatorial District, Victor Ochei, were smashed during the attack. Footages from the scene also showed a counter-mob assaulting some of the alleged attackers apprehended during the melee. Reacting, Ochei called on Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to order immediate investigation into the incident and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted. Ochei, former Speaker, Delta State House of Assembly, described the attack as unacceptable, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of resorting to intimidation instead of issue-based political engagement. “I see no reason why the ruling party should descend so low as to mobilise people to attack the opposition. This is condemnable and unacceptable. “If you are doing well as a party, come out and tell the people what you have achieved to merit re-election instead of resorting to intimidation,” Ochei said. He alleged that more than 30 campaign buses were destroyed by suspected attackers allegedly led by commercial tricycle operators under the supervision of an alleged task force official in charge of commercial tricycles in the state. Ochei urged Oborevwori to call APC members to order, warning that Delta should not be turned into a theatre of political violence. “Delta State should not be turned into a theatre of bloodshed,” he said. Also speaking, Delta State Coordinator of the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement (OK Movement) and one of the organisers of the march, Favour Emerue, said the gathering was peaceful until suspected hoodlums disrupted it. He alleged that some participants sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention in hospitals. “This is not the democracy we fought for. Nigerians are ready to defend their votes in 2027 to ensure that the country works. No Deltan should lose his or her life because of an election,” Emerue said. He warned that the governor would be held responsible if any resident lost their life to political violence, while calling on security agencies to investigate and prosecute those culpable. Emerue disclosed that the organisers had notified the police and met with the Commissioner of Police ahead of the march. item.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. More recently, in October , Fubara and Wike held another reconciliation meeting in Port Harcourt alongside their supporters, in what was seen as an effort to consolidate the rapprochement between the two political camps. item.title: Hunger: Tinubu tackles Atiku, asks how he built university as VP
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has hit back at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and others criticising his administration over hardship and hunger, accusing them of contributing to the problems he inherited. Tinubu spoke on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition presidential campaign rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Responding to those raising concerns about hunger, Tinubu said his administration was working to address the problems left behind by previous governments. “Those people talking of hunger, I’m cleaning the mess they created. Atiku was one of them,” Tinubu said. He then questioned how Atiku, who served as vice president and was involved in economic affairs during the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, was able to establish a university while in office. “Ask him how he built a university while in office as vice president in charge of our economy. Who built the university for him? It’s your money. It’s your effort,” he said. He further questioned Atiku’s moral standing to criticise his administration, describing him as a man lacking the integrity and ethical standards required for public office. Tinubu also expressed appreciation to Rivers residents for the support they gave him during the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his emergence as president. “Thank you for the last election. In 2022, 2023, I looked very hopeless, but you trooped out to support me and gave me the mandate,” Tinubu said. “I’m seeking a second term because you believe in me and that I care for you,” he said. item.title: Tinubu: Yari sets 2.3m votes target for Rivers APC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Director General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Sen. Abdulaziz Yari, on Saturday set a target of 2.3 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in Rivers state in the January 16 election. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt, Yari said the party would mobilize its supporters to achieve the feat. “The message here, we are looking for at least nothing less than 2.3 million votes,” he said. He asked the crowd to raise their hands if they were ready to support the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to deliver Tinubu at that figure. Yari said the figure was within reach, citing voter data he obtained from the coalition’s leaders in the state. “Out of 3.3 million voters registered and about 2.8 million PVCs collected, we should be aiming at nothing less than 2.3 million,” he said. He told the President that Rivers was one of the states from which the party expected “nothing less than 80 percent, by God’s grace.” Yari also took aim at the opposition, saying those seeking power had themselves been in government without achieving anything tangible. “From Atiku, to Peter Obi, to Amaechi, down to vice president Atiku Abubakar. He was elected as a governor before becoming a vice president,” he said. The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, said Rivers was the only state in the South-South that Tinubu won convincingly in 2023, and that the state was ready to repeat the feat. He equally added that under Tinubu, Nigeria now gets more revenue from taxation than from crude oil. National Chairman of the APC, Nentawe Yilwatda, described the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as “the best for now in Nigeria.” “Here, we have the numbers. Here, we have the voters,” he said of Rivers. Senator Magnus Abe, who spoke on behalf of Rivers stakeholders, defended the Rainbow Coalition, whose members, he said, have diverse interests but “whose main interest is to return the president to power.” Abe said he was surprised to hear some party members talking down on the coalition. item.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
item.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw.
